title: Most Adults Cannot Pass This Social Worker Entrance Exam
summary: Ten questions test listening, ethics, safeguarding and real-world support decisions.

landing.intro: The first questions test empathy. Then the situations move into confidentiality, boundaries and decisions where every detail matters.

about.body:
This ten-question entertainment challenge uses broad social-work principles that apply across Tier 1 English-speaking countries. It moves from listening and consent into confidentiality, cultural humility, safeguarding, documentation and professional boundaries.

Choose one answer for each situation. Correctness stays hidden until the final reveal, where the complete answer review is available to unlock.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Answer ten increasingly difficult practice scenarios.
Choose the single most responsible general response.
Reveal your score, then unlock every answer you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited social-work admission, licensing or employment exam, and it is not professional or safeguarding advice. Laws, reporting duties and professional standards vary by location.

stage-1.preAdCopy: Your ten answers have been checked and your professional judgment score is ready to reveal.

profile-1.title: The Practice Standout
profile-1.copy: You balanced empathy, safety and professional responsibility with exceptional accuracy. Even the final autonomy question stayed clear.

profile-2.title: The Social-Work Thinker
profile-2.copy: You passed a challenge that defeats most adults. Your judgment stayed strong from the opening conversation to the final scenario.

profile-3.title: The Thoughtful Advocate
profile-3.copy: You built a strong result across a demanding mix of people and practice skills. A few ethical details kept the pass mark just out of reach.

profile-4.title: The Promising Candidate
profile-4.copy: The listening instincts clicked, while confidentiality and safeguarding proved tougher. The review explains every missed answer.

profile-5.title: The First-Round Applicant

socialworker-q1.question: Which opening question is most likely to help a person explain what support they want?
answers: What would you most like help with today?
Why did you let this happen?
Do you agree that my plan is best?
Can we skip the background and complete the form?

socialworker-q2.question: What is essential for informed consent?
answers: A professional deciding what is best without discussion
The person understands the relevant information and agrees voluntarily
A signed form in every possible situation
Agreement from a family member instead of the person

socialworker-q3.question: Which statement about confidentiality is most accurate?
answers: Information can never be shared for any reason
Everything may be shared with anyone on the support team
Privacy is protected, but serious safety concerns or legal duties may require limited sharing
Confidentiality ends after the first meeting

socialworker-q4.question: Which response best demonstrates cultural humility?
answers: Assume everyone from the same background has similar needs
Avoid discussing culture under all circumstances
Use a standard plan before hearing the person's perspective
Ask about the person's preferences and remain open to correcting your assumptions

socialworker-q5.question: What is a strengths-based assessment most likely to explore?
answers: The person's abilities, resources, relationships and goals as well as their needs
Only the problems listed on a referral
Whether the person agrees with every professional opinion
Which service requires the least documentation

socialworker-q6.question: A person receiving support asks their social worker for a personal loan. What is the best general response?
answers: Lend a small amount but keep it private
Maintain the professional boundary and explore appropriate sources of practical support
Ask another person receiving support to provide it
End all support immediately without explanation

socialworker-q7.question: A conversation raises a credible concern that a child or vulnerable adult may be unsafe. What is the best general next step?
answers: Investigate every detail alone before telling anyone
Ignore it unless physical evidence is available
Record the concern and follow the applicable safeguarding or reporting process promptly
Post an anonymous account online for advice

socialworker-q8.question: Which case note is generally the most appropriate?
answers: A delayed note based mainly on memory
A personal opinion about the person's character
Every detail from the worker's entire day
A timely, relevant and factual record that distinguishes observation from opinion

socialworker-q9.question: When working with other professionals, which information-sharing approach is generally strongest?
answers: Share relevant information lawfully, involve the person where possible and disclose no more than necessary
Send the full record automatically to every service
Never share information even when a serious safety duty applies
Rely only on informal verbal updates

socialworker-q10.question: A capable adult understands the options but declines a voluntary service. What is the best general response?
answers: Pressure them until they agree
Check understanding and immediate safety, explain available options and respect the informed choice unless another legal duty applies
Contact their employer to persuade them
Remove every future route back to support
